analysis:
All changes in this batch are documentation only. Only docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md raises a security-relevant point.

1. prefix-cache.md (hunk @@ -126, head lines ~130-153) adds an 'Unregistered GLM sparse-state candidate' section. It describes the `native-paged-glm5next-full-state-v1` layout and says GLM SSD prefix cache defaults on for `EigenLabs/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-NVFP4-mtp` via `isGLM5NextDefaultModel`. `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0` opts out. GLM is stated to be outside registered coordinator serving models and not qualified. T-041 does not list this model or this standalone, non-coordinator scoping case, so I raised a low-severity finding. The code was not supplied and I could not verify it, so a later pass should check `PrefixCachePolicy+Activation.swift` for how `cacheSalt` is populated when no coordinator is present, and how the KEK, HMAC lookup and TTL apply.

2. model-registry.md adds a raw GLM discovery quotation note. It says discovery uses bounded headers and non-weight sizes, has no generic fallback for a malformed GLM inventory, and supports only the tokenizer shipped in the snapshot. It explicitly says this does not replace catalog or source identity checks, and it introduces no security regression. The linked reference and the implementation (ModelDownloader and the registry scan) were not supplied.

3. inference.md (head lines 1212-1410) adds media-decoder, MiMo composition, Flash-Next ownership and admission, and Bonsai statements. `advertisedContextExceeded` is described as a content-free client error, and the cache-hit bypass is closed. Nothing in it conflicts with the threat model, but the implementation was not examined.

findings.detail: The new prefix-cache.md section says that for the locally selected `EigenLabs/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-NVFP4-mtp`, SSD eligibility defaults on (`PrefixCachePolicy.isGLM5NextDefaultModel`) and `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0` is the opt-out. The same section says the codec adds no qualified cache capability and that GLM is outside the registered coordinator serving models. T-041 describes the encrypted SSD tier as a mandated sign-off for at-rest artifacts. It frames the default-on scope around eligible CBv2 models and coordinator-authored `cacheSalt` account scoping, and it notes a model-ID fallback in standalone mode. A GLM candidate served locally or unregistered would get a new default-on persistent at-rest KV surface. That surface includes the within-TTL TTFT oracle across restarts and the asymmetric full-state payload, without coordinator account scoping. T-041 and SEC-035 do not address this. If the default-on claim matches the code, it should be recorded in T-041 with its scope, or gated behind an explicit opt-in until qualified. The visible text cannot confirm the code behavior, and the change is documentation only.
findings.title: GLM-5.3 Flash candidate documented as SSD prefix-cache default-on while unqualified; T-041 not updated
